question: How do a master's targets become torque on a joint and come back as positions?
tldr: Frame writes the dictionary; physics reads it, then writes actuals back.
answer: The object dictionary sits between two clocks: each process data frame copies the master's outputs into it and the drive's inputs out of it, and each physics step reads the mode and target from it, gives a torque, and writes the new actual position and velocity into it.
why: Frames and physics steps run at different times in different functions; the picture shows that the dictionary is the only thing between them, so the master always reads what the last physics step wrote.

nodes.label: process data frame
nodes.explain: One LRW datagram each cycle: the chip's FMMU puts this drive's slice in its output sync manager (SM2) and takes its inputs from SM3.

nodes.label: Drive::outputs
nodes.tldr: RxPDO bytes into the dictionary, in Op
nodes.explain: Copies SM2 into the objects mapped by 0x1C12 (controlword 0x6040, targets 0x607A/0x60FF/0x6071, mode 0x6060). Only in Operational.

nodes.label: modes, controlword
nodes.tldr: mode runs if supported; state machine steps
nodes.explain: 0x6061 follows 0x6060 when it's CSP, CSV or CST. The controlword moves CiA 402's state machine.

nodes.label: object dictionary
nodes.explain: The drive's CoE objects. Frames and physics steps meet only here: each reads what the other wrote last.

nodes.label: Drive::sense
nodes.explain: The drivetrain's encoder reading, in counts, becomes the actual position and velocity; the torque the motor gave becomes 0x6077, and the target minus position the following error (0x60F4). Then the inputs are refreshed.

nodes.label: Drive::law
nodes.tldr: CSP, CSV or CST torque, up to 0x6072
nodes.explain: In Operation Enabled: CSP is a PD loop on the position error, CSV a P loop on velocity, CST the torque asked. Clamped to the max torque (0x6072). Also runs the watchdog and the following error check.

nodes.label: Drydock::step
nodes.tldr: drivetrain limits torque; MuJoCo moves joint
nodes.explain: The physics step, every 0.5 ms: the drivetrain turns the asked torque into what the motor gives, and MuJoCo moves the joint under it.

nodes.label: Drive::inputs
nodes.tldr: TxPDO objects into SM3, from Safe-Op
nodes.explain: Updates the statusword, then copies the objects mapped by 0x1C13 (statusword, actual position, velocity, torque, mode, error code) into SM3 for the frame to take.
